name: Washington University in St. Louis
header:
Washington University in St. Louis
United States · Mathematics PhD
Rank verification is maintained separately.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• PhD deadline Dec 1; MA Jan 15 is not interchangeable.
• Three-letter maximum; no Interfolio.
• Officially published stipend is old 2024-25 figure.
• Current roster lists Steven Krantz, N. Mohan Kumar, David Wright and Jack Shapiro as emeriti. Silas Johnson
and Karl Schaefer are senior lecturers in number theory; do not assume ordinary research-PhD supervision.
Wanlin Li moved to Vanderbilt in August 2025 and Laura Escobar to UC Santa Cruz in 2024; old WashU profiles
are not evidence of current ordinary adviser availability.
• Faculty below form a verified research-fit shortlist, not a complete census. New-student supervision and 2027
leave/moves must be confirmed; paper dates describe the cited version.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor's or equivalent before enrollment; may apply while unfinished. UChicago degree type qualifies; strong
field preparation and good standing required. [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare final versions before submission; later revisions usually refused. Enter 3 referees; portal questions
determine English exemption. [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Program contact math@wustl.edu; no prior supervisor agreement publicly listed. [s1] [s2]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
gradadmit.washu.edu; application checklist/recommender reminders/receipt rules publicly documented. [s3]
[s4]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Explicit Fall 2027 PhD deadline; funding page rate is 2024-25. [s1] [s5]

English requirement [Standing rule]
DET 125; Gateway 495; IELTS 6.5; TOEFL wording on page mixes scales (new 5.0 and old 90). No superscores.
Confirm exact TOEFL-scale interpretation if testing. [s3]
UChicago English exemption [Unresolved]
Portal assesses prior English academic study and credentials for automatic waiver or documentation. Linked
policy landing page did not expose detailed exemption criteria; completed UChicago degree exemption cannot
be certified from retrieved text. [s3] [s6]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional: not required, may submit. GRE Analytical Writing included in this optional policy. [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required; current page does not separately explain recommendation strength or whether optional math
score is considered. [s2]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Math page gives USD 36,000/12 months plus full tuition for 2024-25 only.2027 amount, health/fee treatment
require confirmation. [s5]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Usually renewed to total 5 years with normal progress. [s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Department says all current full-time doctoral students funded; no citizenship distinction for base university
fellowship stated. Named fellowships have separate eligibility to verify. [s5]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Normal progress; first-year University Fellowship has minimal duties. Later support may be research
assistantship. [s5]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
This particular funding term was not established by the public program/admissions material checked. Obtain
the exact rule in the funding offer or from the graduate coordinator; neither eligibility nor a guaranteed
amount/duration is inferred from silence. [s1] [s2] [s3]

Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Olin-Chancellor's, McDonnell Academy and McNair listed. Their separate applications, eligibility and extra
references/essays need award-specific verification. [s5]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 45, credit card or US-bank electronic check. [s3]

This item remains unverified after checking the public program and graduate-admissions instructions. Confirm

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Roya Beheshti
Rational curves and hypersurfaces; Fano and toric geometry. [faculty1] [currentfaculty]
Professor; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 submitted · Higher-order tangent lines to smooth hypersurfaces
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Matt Kerr
Hodge theory, algebraic cycles and normal functions; arithmetic aspects of motives and Calabi-Yau geometry.
[faculty2] [currentfaculty]
Professor and director of graduate studies; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Three vignettes on hypergeometric normal functions
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Carl Lian
Moduli of curves and maps; Brill-Noether and Hurwitz theory; enumerative geometry and intersection theory.
[faculty3] [currentfaculty]
Assistant Professor at WashU since 2025; formerly at Tufts; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · A Brill-Noether theorem for (toric) surfaces
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.

Complex geometry
Charles Ouyang
Higgs bundles, Riemann surfaces and higher Teichmüller theory; harmonic maps and minimal surfaces.
[faculty4] [currentfaculty]
Assistant Professor; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2024 · Higgs bundles and SYZ geometry
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Gregory Knese
Several complex variables, rational functions and operator/function theory; analytic rather than principally
algebraic geometry. [faculty5] [currentfaculty]
Professor; current appointment verified by 2026-27 roster. Cited CV is May 2024; latest-paper status unverified.
Research evidence: 2024 preprint · Boundary local integrability of rational functions in two variables
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
John E. McCarthy
Complex function theory and operator theory; inner functions, holomorphic dynamics and composition
operators. [faculty6] [faculty6a] [currentfaculty]
Spencer T. Olin Professor; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 online first · A note on composition operators on model spaces
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Brett D. Wick
Several complex variables and complex/harmonic analysis; Cauchy-Szegő and Bergman projections, Corona
problems and operator theory. [faculty8] [currentfaculty]
Robert G. and Maxine W. Scheibe Professor and department chair; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Lp Regularity of the Bergman Projection on the Symmetrized Polydisc
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Representation theory
Martha Precup
Lie theory in algebraic geometry, Hessenberg varieties and related combinatorics. [faculty9] [currentfaculty]
Associate Professor; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Matrix Hessenberg schemes over the minimal sheet
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
John Shareshian
Algebraic and topological combinatorics with connections to Lie geometry and Hessenberg varieties. [faculty10]
[currentfaculty]
Professor per current roster; recent joint paper verified on coauthor Precup’s official publication list. New PhD supervision
availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · K-Orbit closures and Hessenberg varieties
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Yanli Song
Representation theory through noncommutative and symplectic geometry; equivariant index theory and
orbital integrals. [faculty11] [currentfaculty]

Associate Professor; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Higher orbital integrals on motion groups and Mackey deformation
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Xiang Tang
Noncommutative and symplectic geometry with representation-theoretic connections, including orbital
integrals and Mackey deformation. [faculty12] [currentfaculty]
Professor; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Mapping Cone and Morse Theory
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
